final.title: Spot free-tier limits before they interrupt work
final.body:
If you run a small business and use a free-tier tool, the useful question is simple: do you know its quota, and do you check usage before the limit is hit?

That could be a SaaS plan, an API, an email tool, or any service that quietly turns convenience into a bill or a block. The point is not whether the tool is clever. The point is whether you can see the threshold before it becomes a surprise.

One practical next step: pick one tool in your stack and write down three things — the free limit, where usage is visible, and the one reminder that will make you look at it. For some tools, a weekly calendar check is enough. For faster-moving ones, a vendor alert email is better. Keep it boring. Boring is good here.

Why bother? Hitting a free-tier limit can interrupt a workflow, or push you into an unplanned upgrade while you are still deciding whether the process is worth automating. Early visibility does not make that decision for you. It just keeps the decision in your hands.

Start with one tool, one quota, and one check.
